items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Don recorded 4 numbers with a band that included ... Lois Deppe and Don, vocals.

ctx.x: I had heard an orchestra by the name of Lois Dieppe once at Elmwood Town Hall which was another suburb of Cincinnati. In fact Dieppe was the first orchestra that I heard at Elmwood. Dieppe was from Columbus, Ohio, but I think his orchestra had played around Chicago and it was his first time to play in the vicinity of Cincinnati. There was no one in the orchestra that I gave special notice to except Lois who had such a powerful baritone voice that he stood behind the orchestra in back of the pianist and sang…
out their voices, and the orchestra did not have to soften their tone when Deppe sang.

I found out later that the pianist in Deppe's orchestra was a young man by the name of Earl Hines. One night Lois Deppe stopped at the Woodlawn. This Road House did not cater for negroes, but the owner would allow them to come in and say hello to the musicians if they were musicians also. A few days after the visit of Lois Deppe, Edgar Hayes announced that he was leaving to go with Deppe's orchestra who was working somewhere in Cleveland Ohio.
